mechanisms.behavior: Coil 1/plunger and roller linkage swing the bat; extension spring returns it against the adjustable stop. Button 26 is a cabinet command, not bat EOS. The retained table moves directly from BatPress/BatRelease while observing 1; its fallback does not prove physical coil timing.
mechanisms.label: Baseball Bat

mechanisms.behavior: One 14-7959 motor receives three speed branches through A-14381 regulator. It rotates clockwise viewed from left, drives pitch plate through one ball from the six-ball return queue and reports a timing-cam opto 54. Home is arm toward front/beam clear. Slow/medium/fast are branches of one motor, not three mechanisms; ROM errors can follow absent home feedback. Table delays are tuning, not measured cam widths.
mechanisms.label: Three-speed Pitcher

mechanisms.behavior: One under-playfield B-20-9608 magnet deflects slower pitches; fast pitches are little affected. No dedicated position or ball sensor belongs to the magnet. The retained table substitutes lateral force profiles and uses 2 as an acknowledgement, so its force/timing is not a physical calibration.
mechanisms.label: Pitch-path Magnet

mechanisms.behavior: One counter-clockwise motor (viewed from left) and cam raise/lower the center ramp, with timing opto 55. T.12 normally stops with beam clear and reports MOVING/ERROR. Both up/down endpoint semantics require the cam phase/history; clear alone is not proof of which height. Retained model initializes down and supplies modeled cam occlusion; phase windows and timing remain table tuning.
mechanisms.label: Center Up/Down Ramp

mechanisms.behavior: Seven independent A-14452-1..-7 rotating panels actuate their own A-14697 switch wire 41..47 from left to right. Results belong to the lit inserts and ROM. Rear deflector/guide sends the ball into the return trough. No reset solenoid or drop-target latch is fitted; the table's face triggers are contact proxies.
mechanisms.label: Seven Rotating Target Panels

mechanisms.behavior: Left/middle/right shaped ramps behind the target row lead through three separate A-14315/A-14316 optical paths 61/62/63 into gravity returns. These report ball passage, not center-ramp position. Preserve the selected route until the ball clears its beam and joins the return; do not pulse all three for one ball.
mechanisms.label: Three Grandstand / Home Run Returns

mechanisms.behavior: Rear/back-row return 51 and front strike trough 52 join adjustable passive ramps and the lowest trough feeding the single pitcher. Six balls are physical inventory; conserve them rather than create/destroy on every pitch. Height mismatch, guide pressure or a blocked trough can prevent a serve after a command. Sensor locations and exact handoff time remain unmeasured.
mechanisms.label: Six-ball Gravity Return

mechanisms.behavior: Motor 27 drives the original cable/pulley, piston and guide-rod feed under the card magazine, with extension-spring return; optical prize 23 confirms passage and low 27 senses stock. Unjammed 28 is an operator acknowledgement button after clearing a fault, not a healthy-state sensor. Low lamp 28 is normally off, on when low and blinks jam/empty; A.6.06 chooses stop or ignore dispenser errors. One-card gap and chute adjustment prevent double feed/hung cards. The table substitutes held 28=1, pulses 23 on confirmed advancement and models stock; its 15-card capacity and ms windows are tuning, not the factory 1030-card magazine. Revised A-14471-1 and ticket conversion are separate options, not simultaneously fitted hardware.
mechanisms.label: Original Card Dispenser

mechanisms.behavior: Cabinet AE-23-800 coil 7 strikes its mechanical stop and returns; no playfield ball path or sensor belongs to it.
mechanisms.label: Cabinet Knocker

physical.notes: Factory PDF 12 fits A-12697-1; PDF 72 item 51 lists RLY1, part 5580-08994-01, as Relay 4PDT 6VDC5A VS. PDF 118 draws T7 through R208/Q99 to a RELAY DPDT symbol and R/L FLIP RETURN contacts. Preserve the BOM 4PDT versus drawn DPDT readings without inferring additional contacts or fitted flipper loads. wpc.c maps WPC_GILAMPS bit 7 to public 31; native service navigation observes that state. No physical flippers or game-on output 19 are claimed.
Constant zero public WPC state channel: core_getSol remaps only the three WPC_GILAMPS state bits to 29-31. No fourth state bit or fitted physical load exists at public 32.
